content.user_title: Map Large Projects Into Issue Tickets
content.value_statement: Large efforts lose context when one agent session cannot hold every decision. Wayfinder turns the work into a shared issue map with focused tickets and recorded decisions.
actual_capabilities: Defines a map issue that records the destination, notes, decisions, unknown areas, and out-of-scope work.
Structures child tickets around one decision or investigation that fits a single agent session.
Classifies tickets as research, prototype, grilling, or task work.
Guides agents to claim one frontier ticket before starting work.
Explains how to record resolutions and update the map after each ticket closes.
limitations: Requires an issue tracker or a local markdown tracker convention.
Plans decisions by default and does not complete the full project deliverable.
Assumes related skills are available when grilling or domain modeling is needed.
Does not enforce tracker permissions, assignments, or dependency links by itself.

use_cases.title: Plan a Technical Migration
use_cases.description: Turn a broad migration into decision tickets, dependency links, and a visible frontier for the engineering team.

use_cases.title: Shape an Ambiguous Product Initiative

use_cases.title: Organize Course Content Discovery
use_cases.description: Map lessons, unknown topic areas, and required prototypes before writing the final material.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with an unclear project idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder to chart a map for this idea: [describe the project]. First help define the destination and first frontier tickets.

prompt_templates.title: Create First Tickets
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert known questions into issue tracker work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder to create the initial ticket set for this destination: [destination]. Separate decisions, unknown areas, and out-of-scope items.

prompt_templates.title: Work One Ticket
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder on this map: [map link]. Pick one unblocked, unclaimed frontier ticket, claim it, resolve it, and update the map.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Complex Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Advance a map with dependencies and changing scope.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder to review this map: [map link]. Identify newly specified tickets, obsolete tickets, dependency changes, and decisions to record.

output_examples.input: A team needs to modernize an old billing workflow but does not know the risks yet.
output: A map issue with the migration destination and standing notes.
Research tickets for current billing behavior and vendor constraints.
Prototype tickets for risky workflow changes.
Out-of-scope notes for work outside the migration destination.

output_examples.input: A user provides an existing map and asks the agent to continue.
output: The agent loads the map summary, then selects one unblocked ticket.
The ticket is claimed before work starts.
The final answer is recorded on the ticket, then the map receives a short decision pointer.

best_practices: Define the destination before creating tickets so scope stays clear.
Resolve only one ticket per session to keep decisions traceable.
Keep detailed answers on tickets and place only short pointers on the map.
anti_patterns: Do not use the map as a full storage document for every ticket answer.
Do not create tickets for unknown areas before the question is clear.
Do not complete delivery work when the map only needs planning decisions.

faq.question: What does Wayfinder create?
faq.answer: It creates a planning map and child issue tickets that track decisions, unknown areas, and scope boundaries.

faq.question: Does it finish the project work?
faq.answer: No. It plans the route by default and stops when the remaining work is clear.

faq.question: Can it use GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes, if the repository issue tracker supports the needed labels, child links, and dependency relationships.

faq.question: How does it support parallel work?
faq.answer: Tickets are claimed by assignment, so other sessions can skip claimed work and choose open frontier tickets.

faq.question: When should I use a task ticket?
faq.answer: Use a task ticket when a concrete action must happen before a decision can be made.

faq.question: What happens when scope changes?
faq.answer: The map records out-of-scope work and updates or closes tickets that no longer support the destination.
